chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Muskān, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated to me; he said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام

about a junub man who comes upon a small amount of water on the road and wants to perform ghusl from it, but does not have with him a vessel with which to scoop from it, and his hands are dirty. He said: He puts in his hand, performs wudu (ablution), and performs ghusl.
This is from what Allah, the Exalted, has said: “He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship.”

Thus, the correct way to understand this report is that he should take the water from the pool with his hand and not enter it himself, and perform ghusl by pouring the water over the body. His statement عليه السلام, “and his hands are dirty,” indicates the filth upon them in the sense of grime, not najasah, because najasah would spoil the water for use upon the body when it is a small amount, as we have already explained.

key_terms.النَّجَاسَةِ: ritual impurity that contaminates the water
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in a state requiring ghusl due to janabah
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْقَلِيلِ: a small quantity of water subject to contamination rulings
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: hardship or undue difficulty in religious law
key_terms.قَذِرَتَانِ: dirty with ordinary filth or grime

ai.seo_question: What should a junub person do if he finds only a small amount of water and has no vessel to draw from it?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for a junub person who finds only a small amount of water and has no vessel to draw it with. It indicates a facilitative ruling based on the Qur'anic principle that there is no hardship in religion, while clarifying that the dirt on the hands refers to ordinary grime, not ritual impurity that would contaminate the water.
